title: Jalen Brunson: Game 6 in Philly
description: Forty-one points, a Villanova dime, and a go-ahead three—Go Deep into a road clincher that sent the Garden into summer early.
imageHint: A point guard in blue and orange willing a road clincher

questions.question: In Game 6 of the 2024 first round, which Knicks guard scored 41 points with 12 assists on the road to close the series?
questions.explanation: Fourteen of those points came in the fourth. It was his fourth straight playoff game with 39-plus—company only a handful of legends have kept.

questions.question: Brunson's biggest dime that night found which Villanova teammate for a go-ahead three with 24.4 seconds left?
questions.explanation: Hart was waiting up top. The three made it 114–111. Free throws finished Philly; the Garden heard it from 90 miles away.

questions.question: Hart's go-ahead three sealed a first-round win over which Joel Embiid–led franchise?
questions.explanation: Series: 4–2. Embiid had 39 and 13 in the finale and still walked off. Next up for New York: Indiana in the conference semis.

questions.question: Earlier against those 76ers, Brunson's 47-point Game 4 broke which Knick's 1984 playoff scoring record?
questions.explanation: King's mark had stood forty years. Brunson also added 10 assists that night—and shrugged afterward: he'd think about the record when he retired.

questions.question: Bernard King's old Knicks playoff high that Brunson passed was how many points?
questions.explanation: Brunson 47, King 46. One point. The kind of number Garden lifers can recite without looking it up.

deeperMode.title: Go Deeper: Before the Garden
deeperMode.description: The second-round steal and the dad who ran the point

questions.question: Before the Knicks, Dallas drafted Brunson where in 2018—a pick that looks absurd now?
questions.hint: Second round, after two Villanova titles

questions.question: Brunson's father—who ran the point in the NBA, including a stop in New York—is named what?
questions.hint: Nine seasons, eight teams, later a coach

easterEgg.title: 56 in a state final
easterEgg.text: At Stevenson High in Illinois, Brunson dropped 56 in an IHSA finals game—a state-final scoring record—against a team featuring future No. 1 pick Jahlil Okafor. The Garden version was always in there.
